facts.fact: Paratus says Powertel Communications and Paratus Zimbabwe signed a PPP agreement in June 2025 to jointly invest in high-capacity long-distance fibre in Zimbabwe, the Botswana-Zimbabwe-Zambia corridor, with an IRU between them.
Paratus says the second phase, connecting Bulawayo and Livingstone (Zambia), is due to be lit in September 2026 to complete the three-country corridor.

Paratus and Powertel announce the first phase, Plumtree to Bulawayo, is live and carrying traffic with 800 Gbps equipped capacity, as the first active Paratus-connected fibre route into Zimbabwe linking it to Botswana, Zambia and South Africa; no other country's operator or traffic figure is given.

systems.platform: DWDM fibre, over 10 Tbps capable, 800 Gbps equipped
systems.owner: Powertel Communications (planned, built, owned and operated) with Paratus Zimbabwe under an IRU
